name: Shell

summary.text: Shell is a multinational oil and gas company headquartered in the United Kingdom, formerly Royal Dutch Shell. Internal documents made public in 2018 by Dutch journalist Jelmer Mommers and the Climate Investigations Center include a 1988 report marked confidential, 'The Greenhouse Effect', produced by Shell's Greenhouse Effect Working Group, and a 1991 public film, 'Climate of Concern', made by the company's film and video unit. In May 2021 the Hague District Court ordered Shell to cut its emissions 45% by 2030 against 2019 levels; the Hague Court of Appeal set that order aside on 12 November 2024, and the Dutch Supreme Court heard a further appeal in May 2026. Shell is a defendant in U.S. state and municipal climate-deception suits, including the City and County of Honolulu's 2020 case, which the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review in January 2025.

facts.claim: A 1988 Shell report titled 'The Greenhouse Effect', marked confidential and written by members of the company's Greenhouse Effect Working Group on the basis of a 1986 study, warned that by the time global warming became detectable it could be too late to take effective countermeasures. The report also describes an internal Shell climate science program dating to 1981.
facts.quote: However, by the time the global warming becomes detectable it could be too late to take effective countermeasures to reduce the effects or even to stabilize the situation.

sources.title: What 30 Years of Documents Show Shell Knew About Climate Science
Shell Climate Documents

facts.claim: In 1991 Shell's film and video unit released a public documentary, 'Climate of Concern', about global warming. According to E&E News, the film stated that waiting for ironclad proof before acting would be irresponsible. The film was made public again in 2017 by the Dutch outlet De Correspondent.
facts.quote: waiting for ironclad proof would be irresponsible.

sources.title: Documents show Shell grappled with climate change years ago
If Shell knew climate change was dire 25 years ago, why still business as usual today?

facts.claim: DeSmog reported that a 1994 Shell document, not marked confidential, focused on the arguments of climate skeptics and questioned climate models, in contrast to the company's 1988 confidential report. DeSmog also reported that Shell took 16 years from its internal study of climate risk to warn shareholders of that risk.
facts.quote: A 1994 document, which was not marked confidential, focused on the arguments of climate skeptics and questioned climate models.

sources.title: What 30 Years of Documents Show Shell Knew About Climate Science
Exclusive: Shell Took 16 Years To Warn Shareholders of Climate Risks, Despite Knowing in Private All Along

facts.claim: In May 2021 the Hague District Court ordered Shell to reduce its scope 1, 2 and 3 CO2 emissions by 45% by 2030 relative to 2019. On 12 November 2024 the Hague Court of Appeal set that order aside, holding that although Dutch law imposes a duty of care on Shell to reduce emissions, Shell cannot be bound to a 45% reduction or any other specific percentage, and dismissed Milieudefensie's claim in its entirety.
facts.quote: Although the Court reaffirmed that Dutch law imposes a standard of care on Shell to reduce its emissions, it held that Shell cannot be bound to a 45% reduction standard (or any other percentage), as this standard does not apply to individual sectors or countries.

facts.claim: Milieudefensie appealed the 2024 Court of Appeal decision to the Dutch Supreme Court, which heard the case on 22 May 2026; a ruling was reported to be expected in the first half of 2027. Milieudefensie has also announced a separate claim seeking to stop Shell from developing new oil and gas resources.
facts.quote: The hearing will be the first time a country's top court has considered a company's civil duty of care to reduce emissions in order to tackle dangerous climate change.

facts.claim: Shell is a defendant, with ExxonMobil, BP, ConocoPhillips, BHP, Marathon and Chevron, in a 2020 suit by the City and County of Honolulu and the Honolulu Board of Water Supply alleging deceptive conduct about climate change. On 13 January 2025 the U.S. Supreme Court denied certiorari in Sunoco LP v. Honolulu and Shell PLC v. Honolulu, leaving the case in Hawaii state court; the Hawaii Supreme Court had found that the Clean Air Act does not preempt the state-law claims. The allegations have not been decided on the merits.
facts.quote: Today the Supreme Court denied certiorari in Sunoco LP v. Honolulu and Shell PLC v. Honolulu, two petitions from oil companies seeking High Court intervention in a state-law-based climate case in Hawaii.

facts.claim: In April 2019 Shell published its first review of its trade association memberships, assessing 19 industry groups. It found alignment with nine, some misalignment with nine, and material misalignment with one, the American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers, which it said it would leave in 2020 because AFPM had not stated support for the goal of the Paris Agreement. Shell named the American Petroleum Institute and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce among groups it disagreed with on climate but said it would engage further with them.
facts.quote: AFPM has not stated support for the goal of the Paris Agreement. Shell supports the goal of the Paris Agreement.

connections.claim: Shell is a member of the American Petroleum Institute. In its April 2019 review of 19 trade associations, Shell listed API among groups with which it had some misalignment on climate policy but said it would engage further with them rather than leave.
connections.quote: Shell also named nine other groups that it disagreed with, including the American Petroleum Institute and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, but said it would "engage further" with them.

connections.claim: Shell is a member of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. Its April 2019 trade association review listed the Chamber among groups with which it had some misalignment on climate policy but said it would engage further with them.
connections.quote: Shell also named nine other groups that it disagreed with, including the American Petroleum Institute and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, but said it would "engage further" with them.

connections.claim: Royal Dutch Shell was a member of the Global Climate Coalition, the industry group formed in 1989 that opposed the Kyoto Protocol; Shell Oil is named among its founding members.
connections.quote: Other prominent members included BP, Royal Dutch Shell, DuPont, Ford Motor Company, Daimler Chrysler, Texaco, General Motors, and Exxon.

sources.title: Global Climate Coalition
Business nonsense

connections.claim: Shell announced in April 2019 that it would leave the American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers in 2020, citing material misalignment on climate policy, including AFPM's lack of stated support for the Paris Agreement goal and its opposition to carbon pricing.
connections.quote: The company said it had found "material misalignment" over climate policy with the American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers (AFPM) and would quit the body in 2020.

sources.title: Shell to leave AFPM in 2020 over climate 'misalignment'

connections.claim: Milieudefensie sued Shell in the Netherlands, winning a 2021 district court order for a 45% emissions cut by 2030 that the Hague Court of Appeal set aside on 12 November 2024. Milieudefensie appealed to the Dutch Supreme Court, which heard the case in May 2026.
connections.quote: The court dismissed Milieudefensie's claim in its entirety.

connections.claim: The City and County of Honolulu and the Honolulu Board of Water Supply sued Shell and other oil companies in 2020 in Hawaii state court, alleging deceptive conduct about climate change. The U.S. Supreme Court denied Shell's petition for review on 13 January 2025. The allegations remain untested.
connections.quote: The suit was filed in 2020 by the city and county of Honolulu and the Honolulu Board of Water Supply, a semi-autonomous city agency.
